author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says Tehran remains in close contact with mediators over efforts to end the war with the United States, insisting that diplomacy still has a chance to succeed. Araghchi says Iran is reviewing proposals that could allow its seven-day plan to be implemented in less than a week. Tehran maintains that it is prepared for further confrontation while keeping diplomatic channels open. Iranian officials say the main concern is not how quickly an agreement can be reached, but whether the country's demands will be met, including an end to the wider regional war, the lifting of the naval blockade and measures addressing sanctions and frozen Iranian assets. Recent diplomatic engagements have involved Qatar, Russia, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, although Tehran has disclosed few details of the discussions. Iranian officials are also seeking firm guarantees that any interim or permanent agreement will be implemented, amid continuing mistrust. 

Al Jazeera
title: Iran says diplomacy remains possible as mediators discuss plan to end war with US

description: Tens of thousands of people have fled southern Ethiopia into neighbouring Kenya after fighting erupted between forces from the Oromia and Somali regions in the border town of Moyale. The clashes have reignited a decades-long dispute over territory, grazing land and water resources, forcing families to abandon their homes and seek shelter in schools and other temporary facilities. The Kenya Red Cross says it is organising assistance for at least 30,000 displaced people, many of whom have gone days without food. Refugees describe fleeing under cover of darkness and struggling to access food, shelter, clothing and medical treatment, particularly for pregnant women and children. The conflict has erupted repeatedly since Ethiopia redrew its internal boundaries along ethnic lines in the 1990s, leaving the disputed border around Moyale unresolved. description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has delivered a defiant speech at Likud party headquarters, claiming his party is Israel’s largest and arguing that the right-wing bloc has a decisive majority.

Netanyahu highlighted Israel’s military operations in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, describing them as major security achievements. He vowed to continue working with US President Donald Trump to confront what he called the Iranian threat.

He also rejected the prospect of forming a government dependent on Arab parties, calling for a united right-wing coalition.

However, early exit polls indicate that neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition has secured a clear parliamentary majority. Final results and coalition negotiations will determine who can form Israel’s next government.
